title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-03-31
content:
Perf benchmarking sync notes — 2026-03-31
Attendees: Aditi Rao (notes), Miguel Torres, Claire Bennett, Ravi Singh, Elena Kuznetsova, + SRE drop-in: Jonah Lee

High-level summary:
- We observed a regression in end-to-end streaming generation latency and a throughput drop on batch workloads after the runtime patch (commit 1a2b3c4) merged 2026-03-29.
- Impacted: hosted API and dedicated pools running models with long KV cache lifetimes (context ~512+).
- Immediate mitigation: reverted two kernel selection changes in canary (PR #2988) — reduced p95 by ~12% in canary, awaiting broader rollout plan.

Recent test runs (environment: g5dn-like, inference image v2026.03.29, perf harness: perf-run-2026-03-30):
- Streaming synth workload (model: rw-ggml-13b-quant-v2, seq_len=512, concurrency=8, token_streaming=true):
  - baseline (pre-change, commit 0f9e8d): p50=28ms/token, p95=110ms/token, avg throughput=720 tokens/s per GPU
  - post-change (commit 1a2b3c4): p50=36ms/token (+28%), p95=124ms/token (+13%), throughput=620 tokens/s (-14%)
  - canary (reverted kernels, PR #2988): p50=30ms/token, p95=118ms/token, throughput=690 tokens/s
- Batch dense workload (model: rw-t5-large, seq_len=128, batch_size=8):
  - baseline: qps=950 req/s, p95 latency=210ms
  - post-change: qps=820 req/s (-14%), p95=260ms (+24%)
- KV-cache heavy replay (prefix cache hit rate ~85%):
  - observed increased GC stalls during KV reuse in post-change runs; suspect changes to KV buffer eviction heuristics + new kernel path interacting poorly with small allocations.

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Kernel selection logic change (1a2b3c4) added a fallback path that uses a different matmul kernel for small-width workloads; that kernel has worse memory locality for streaming access patterns and increases CPU scheduling pressure during async copy.
- Combined with slightly altered batch coalescing timing, we see more frequent small CUDA memcpy ops (many <4KB) which increases overhead and reduces effective throughput.
- SRE telemetry shows small-but-spiky host CPU utilization rising from median 18% -> 34% during streaming tests.

Repro steps (so engineering + perf can reproduce locally):
1) Checkout commit 1a2b3c4 (branch: perf/kernel-selection-experiment).
2) Build image: docker build -t rw/perf:v2026-03-29 .
3) Run perf harness: ./perf/run.sh --model rw-ggml-13b-quant-v2 --seq 512 --concurrency 8 --streaming --tokens 20000 --env g5dn-sim
4) Collect traces: perf-collector --trace-type=nvtx,hostcpu --out /tmp/trace-1a2b3c4
5) Compare to baseline (commit 0f9e8d) using perf/compare.py --left /tmp/trace-0f9e8d --right /tmp/trace-1a2b3c4
6) Validate canary revert (PR #2988) by repeating above on canary image v2026-03-31-canary.

Logs & artifacts produced:
- perf-run-2026-03-30/streaming-rw-ggml-13b-1a2b3c4.trace (NVTX + host CPU) — uploaded to Confluence page linked above
- heap/dumps: kv-alloc-sample-2026-03-30.log (shows small alloc churn)
- kernel-profiles: kernel-profile-1a2b3c4.tsv

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Miguel: finish full-spectrum kernel microbench suite across shapes (1x, 2x, 4x widths) and upload results to Confluence. ETA: 2026-04-02 (blocked: need access to wide-shape GPU runner)
- Claire: run memalloc/GC sampling with slower cadence to confirm small allocation churn hypothesis; instrument async copy counters. ETA: 2026-04-01
- Ravi: coordinate canary rollout plan. Start limited canary (10% traffic) for PR #2988 revert with auto-rollback at 10% p95 regression. ETA: 2026-04-01
- Elena: create JIRA ticket PERF-4123 with prioritized checklist and attach traces, logs. ETA: 2026-03-31 (in progress)
- Jonah (SRE): add host CPU percentile alert for streaming nodes (trigger at host_cpu_p95 > 40% for 5m). ETA: 2026-04-02
- Aditi: update perf-run dashboard with baseline vs canary comparison panels + brief notes for weekly eng sync. ETA: 2026-04-01

Open questions / discussion items:
- Is the new kernel path providing benefits for other workloads (long sequences) that justify the degradation for streaming? Need end-to-end win/loss matrix.
- Could batching/coalescing be tuned dynamically by workload classifier instead of using global kernel selection heuristic? (Ravi to explore feasibility)
- Should we add microbench CI gating for small memcpy counts per sequence to prevent regressions slipping in?

Decisions made in this meeting:
- Temporary mitigation: merge revert PR (already in canary) and start limited canary rollout once Claire confirms memalloc behavior does not regress other workloads (Ravi + Claire to coordinate).
- Add kernel microbench suite to CI infra as a medium-term requirement (backlog item).

Next sync:
- Weekly perf sync stands next Tuesday 2026-04-07 10:00 PT (standup-style, 30m). Focus: canary rollout results, microbench outcomes, and any further regressions discovered.

Notes to self:
- Keep an eye on related PRs: PR #2992 (async-copy-optimizations) — may conflict with revert if both touch kernel selection; coordinate PR owners.
- Tag customer-impacting incidents if we see >=25% p95 delta on hosted API for a 30-min window.

End of notes.
